subject: Mutual action plan: Veridian capacity reservation & gating checkpoints

Subject: Mutual action plan - capacity reservation & gating checkpoints (Veridian)

Hi Claire / Veridian procurement team,

Thanks again for a productive demo last week. Per our conversation, I put together a concise MAP so we can align on acceptance gates, procurement lead times, and an initial GPU pool sizing approach that lets you ramp safely into production. Attached: VERIDIAN_MAP_CAPACITY_OUTLINE.pdf and MAP-capacity-checkpoints.xlsx (outline + editable checkpoints).

High-level proposal (summary):
- Initial evaluation phase (POC): 2 weeks — small dedicated pool (staging) to run SLO tests and integration flows.
- Performance validation: 1 week — throughput/latency stress test with your representative prompt set.
- Production tranche 1: 8 GPUs (H100-equivalent) reserved for 30-day canary.
- Production tranche 2 (scale): additional 24 GPUs after acceptance (to reach 32 total) — staggered delivery by tranche to reduce risk.

Lead time expectations (prelim):
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool in our hosted environment): provisioning & routing configuration: ~2–3 weeks after signature and payment authorization.
- Redwood Private (customer VPC / on-prem): procurement + delivery + install: typically 8–12 weeks depending on vendor queue and site readiness; add 2–3 weeks for validation and security onboarding.

Acceptance gates (examples in the spreadsheet):
1) POC sign-off — functional integration and data-flow checks
2) Performance gate — p95 latency target and tokens/sec throughput validated against baseline prompts
3) Security/compliance gate — access controls, network allowlist, and basic audit logging verified
4) Commercial gate — invoicing milestone and commitment to tranche 2

Open questions for you to confirm so we can lock timelines:
- Do you prefer H100-equivalent instances or a mixed pool (some A100/8-bit quant for cost)?
- Any internal blackout dates or procurement approvals that will affect the 8–12 week on-prem window?
- Who on your side will own the acceptance test sign-off (name + email)?

Next steps I suggest: sign the MAP spreadsheet (editable), we lock the provisional tranche schedule, and we schedule a short runbook review with Priyom (infrastructure) and Marissa (onboarding) this week.

Thanks,

Alex Martinez

Alex — thanks for the summary and the files. A few clarifying items from our side before we commit to dates: 

1) Lead times: the 8–12 week window for on-prem is workable but procurement has a typical approval cycle that takes ~3 weeks. We need the MAP to show exact milestones that trigger purchase orders.

2) Sizing: Veridian's initial traffic estimate suggests we might need a slightly larger production baseline (targeting 40–48 GPUs at steady state). Can you provide a short cost delta for 32 vs 48 GPUs (hosted vs private)?

3) Acceptance owner: I am assigning our infra lead, Daniel Park (daniel.park@veridian.ai), for test sign-off. Please include him on next steps.

Procurement note (procurement@veridian.ai): please confirm required PO lead time and any supply constraints we should be aware of.

If we can see a clear timeline with gating-triggered purchase events, procurement can attempt to expedite. Also please confirm whether Redwood's Dedicated can serve as an interim bridge while on-prem hardware is in transit.

Best,

Hi team — quick technical readout to help shape the MAP checkpoints and lead times. Ill keep this short.

POC & Validation approach:
- Staging pool: 4 GPUs (H100-equivalent) in Dedicated for 2 weeks to run full integration and baseline throughput tests. This gives us realistic p95 latency and tokens/sec numbers with your workload.
- For canary, recommend 8 GPUs (H100-equivalent) in production with traffic shadowing for 7–14 days. If metrics hold, scale by tranches of +8 or +16 depending on observed headroom.

Sizing guidance:
- Your traffic estimate pointing to 40–48 GPUs steady-state implies we should plan tranches: 8 -> 24 -> 40 (three tranches). Starting at 8 for canary reduces wasted reserved capacity if you need tuning.

Lead time specifics:
- Hosted Dedicated: we can allocate reserved capacity in our hosted environment in 10–14 business days after billing/contract is complete (we have pre-warmed pools for many customers).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): hardware procurement (vendor lead) is the dominant factor. Best-case vendor lead for H100-class parts is ~6–8 weeks today; add 2–4 weeks for on-site integration, network/security onboarding, and acceptance tests. That totals ~8–12 weeks depending on vendor queue and site readiness.

Acceptance criteria (metrics we will measure in the MAP):
- Functional: API integration pass/fail per representative flows
- Performance: p95 latency <= 300ms on target prompts; sustained target throughput (tokens/sec) at 80% of predicted concurrency
- Cost/regression: token cost per 1M tokens not deviating >15% from expected baseline in staging

Operational notes:
- We can use Dedicated as an interim bridge if Veridian prefers to run production traffic earlier; that requires a billing commitment and will shorten your effective time-to-prod while private hardware arrives.
- For private installs, please surface any local compliance requirements so we can pre-configure KMS and audit logging templates.

Ill sync with Marissa to build the MAP milestones into the spreadsheet and pin owners + dates.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
